title: The inverse self-commutator cost at inertia $(m,n)$: ordered-layering bounds, interlacing chains, and the Horn tiles that certify them
abstract: For a traceless Hermitian $F\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ let $\kappa_d(F)=\tfrac12\min\{\|C\|_{HS}^2:CC^*-C^*C=2F\}$. On the inertia-$(m,n)$ stratum ($m$ positive and $n$ negative eigenvalues, $z$ zeros) we prove three results valid for all $m,n,z$: a dimension-free lower bound $\kappa_d\ge\operatorname{cost}(L)$ for every ordered full-capacity layering $L$, certified by Lidskii–Wielandt and Weyl inequalities alone; an exact additive formula on the aligned-spike cone, where an optimizer is a direct sum of weighted shifts; and the closed form $\kappa_d=\operatorname{cost}(L_k)$ on explicit full-dimensional regions $R_k$, $1\le k\le m-n+1$, obtained from one rank-one interlacing step. Open question 1 of the inertia-$(m,2)$ paper is refuted by an exact weak-duality certificate: at inertia $(5,4)$ a Horn tile with $n=4$ boxes is necessary, and one valid form cannot be certified using Pieri-shaped tiles alone. The $d=8$ rank-onset example is explained by a late negative. Conjectures for general $(m,n)$ are stated with their numerical evidence.
